newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Court puts Belgian Clabecq in receivership.
newsitem.headline: Court puts Belgian Clabecq in receivership.

text.p: A Belgian commercial court on Friday placed troubled steel maker Forges de Clabecq into receivership, technically declaring the company bankrupt, Belga news agency reported.

"The workers will be given their notice to quit but activities will for now continue," a spokesman for the Walloon Region, which was the company's biggest shareholder and creditor, told Reuters. "Orders are good for the first quarter (of 1997)."

Belga reported the court had appointed four receivers to run the company. They would re-employ as many of the 1,800 strong workforce as they thought necessary. Belgian radio later said 1,350 of the workers might be re-employed.

Clabecq filed for bankruptcy in mid-December after the European Commission rejected a 1.5 billion Belgian franc ($47 million) rescue plan by the Walloon Region, which then withdrew its support for the firm.

But on December 24 the court ruled against declaring Clabecq bankrupt because two experts said the company was still viable and that judging by its order book it could survive in its current form until the middle of 1997.
Friday's ruling was based on another expert's report which assumed as its starting point a full resumption of work from January 6 and the start-up of the furnace from January 4.

Clabecq shares, currently suspended, were last quoted at 76 francs on December 19. Bid and ask prices were indicated at seven francs but the actual decline had been limited by a bourse rule capping the movement in cash market shares at 10 percent below or above the previous close.
A spokesman for the Brussls Stock Exchange was not immediately available to say if trade would now resume.
